full_text_en:
Maoming Grain Bureau Grain and Oil Materials Company v. Maoming Supply and Marketing Cooperative Union Railway Special Line Business Department — Retrial of Dispute over Transportation Contract

Applicant for Retrial: Guangdong Province Maoming Supply and Marketing Cooperative Union Railway Special Line Business Department.

Legal Representative: Mo Mouliang, Manager.

Agent ad litem: Zhan Kejian, lawyer from Guangxi Railway Law Firm.

Opposing Party: Guangdong Province Maoming Grain Bureau Grain and Oil Materials Company.

Legal Representative: Liang Shaolun, General Manager.

Agent ad litem: Cheng Ke, cadre of Guangdong Province Maoming Grain Bureau Grain and Oil Materials Company.

Agent ad litem: Fan Liqiang, lawyer from Guangdong Province Maoming Henghe Law Firm.

The applicant for retrial, Guangdong Province Maoming Supply and Marketing Cooperative Union Railway Special Line Business Department (hereinafter referred to as the Supply Cooperative Line), due to a dispute with the opposing party, Guangdong Province Maoming Grain Bureau Grain and Oil Materials Company (hereinafter referred to as the Grain Company), over a claim for compensation for goods in storage, appealed against the civil judgment (1994) Yue Fa Jing Yi Shang Zi No. 155 of the Guangdong High People's Court and applied to the Supreme People's Court for a retrial. Upon examination, the Supreme People's Court held that the nature of the case was incorrectly determined in the original judgment, and therefore, in accordance with Article 177, Paragraph 2, and Article 183 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, ordered that this case be tried by the Supreme People's Court.

The Supreme People's Court found through trial: In May 1993, the Grain Company purchased 130 sets of Changzheng brand automobile tires from Liaoning Tire Factory, and the parties agreed that Liaoning Tire Factory would arrange for consignment. On June 5 of the same year, Liaoning Tire Factory handled the transportation procedures for consigning the 130 sets of tires to Maoming Railway Station at the Railway Bureau's Chaoyang West Station, with an insured value of RMB 139,000 for the goods. When filling in the consignee column on the consignment note, the factory abbreviated "Maoming Grain Bureau Grain and Oil Materials Company" as "Guangdong Maoming Grain and Oil Materials Company". On June 17, the goods arrived at Maoming Railway Station, and the station, in accordance with its agreement with the Supply Cooperative Line, allocated the freight cars to the Supply Cooperative Line for unloading, and the two parties completed the handover procedures. On the same day, the Supply Cooperative Line issued a notice to the Grain Company to collect the goods. On June 19, when the Grain Company went to Maoming Railway Station with the pickup certificate to complete the procedures for collecting the goods, it was unable to do so because the consignee on the consignment note did not match the actual consignee. On June 20, the Grain Company, as required by Maoming Railway Station, issued a certificate and completed the goods collection procedures, paid the Supply Cooperative Line for line usage, temporary storage, unloading, and other fees, and then went to the Supply Cooperative Line's warehouse to collect the goods, only to learn that the goods had been fraudulently obtained by an impostor on June 19. Investigation revealed that the consignment note held by the impostor was forged. The Grain Company then filed a lawsuit with the Maoming Intermediate People's Court, demanding that the Supply Cooperative Line compensate for the loss of goods of RMB 151,400, interest of RMB 40,000, and compensation of RMB 50,000.

The Maoming Intermediate People's Court held in its trial: The Supply Cooperative Line is an enterprise specialized in cargo transfer, storage, and warehousing services. Maoming Railway Station allocated the tires, which it had carried and were owned by the Grain Company, to the Supply Cooperative Line's warehouse for storage. The Supply Cooperative Line fulfilled its warehousing obligations and collected line usage fees and temporary storage fees, thus establishing a warehousing and storage relationship between the parties. The Supply Cooperative Line should bear liability for the loss of the stored goods due to improper storage and for the resulting loss to the Grain Company due to its inability to supply goods to its downstream buyers. The court therefore ordered the Supply Cooperative Line to compensate the Grain Company RMB 201,400 plus interest on the value of the goods. The Supply Cooperative Line, dissatisfied with this judgment, appealed to the Guangdong High People's Court.

The Guangdong High People's Court held in its final instance: The Grain Company purchased automobile tires from Liaoning Tire Factory and entrusted Liaoning Tire Factory with the consignment. After the goods arrived at Maoming Station, they were allocated by Maoming Station to the Supply Cooperative Line's warehouse for storage. After receiving the goods, the Supply Cooperative Line immediately notified the Grain Company to pay and collect the goods. The Grain Company paid the line usage, temporary storage, and warehouse release fees in a timely manner, thus establishing a warehousing and storage relationship between the parties. As the bailee, the Supply Cooperative Line should be responsible for the stored goods. The responsibility for the goods being fraudulently obtained lies with the Supply Cooperative Line. The Supply Cooperative Line should bear liability for the loss of the goods and the resulting loss to the Grain Company due to its inability to supply goods to its downstream buyers. The court affirmed the original judgment and dismissed the appeal.

The Supply Cooperative Line, dissatisfied with the above judgment of the Guangdong High People's Court, appealed to the Supreme People's Court, arguing: This case is a dispute over mistaken delivery in a cargo transportation contract. The defendant should be Maoming Railway Station. The fraudulent obtaining was caused by a third party forging a consignment note to take the goods. The Supply Cooperative Line merely performed the delivery obligation on behalf of Maoming Railway Station and should not bear liability. There was never any legal relationship of warehousing and storage or agency for receiving goods between the Supply Cooperative Line and the Grain Company. The judgments of the first and second instance courts that characterized the case as a warehousing and storage contract dispute and so ruled were erroneous.

The Grain Company responded: The Supply Cooperative Line, as an enterprise specialized in cargo transfer, storage, and warehousing services, cannot avoid civil liability for the damages arising from its use of the special line for warehousing and storage services simply because the special line is part of the railway. When Maoming Railway Station delivered the goods to the Supply Cooperative Line's warehouse, the transportation of the goods was completed. The Supply Cooperative Line had already proceeded to store the goods, and its act of collecting fees had established a warehousing and storage relationship with the Grain Company. In the first and second instances, the Supply Cooperative Line never denied its liability to compensate the Grain Company for the loss of goods, nor did it apply to add Maoming Railway Station as a defendant. The facts found in the first and second instances were clear, the procedures were lawful, and the application of law was correct.

After trial, the Supreme People's Court held: After Liaoning Tire Factory handled the consignment procedures for the tires at the Railway Bureau's Chaoyang West Station, the carrier's obligation was to transport the tires to the destination station in accordance with the contract and deliver them to the consignee named on the consignment note. The temporary storage of the goods between arrival at the destination station and delivery to the consignee is part of the carrier's obligations under the transportation contract. In this case, the consignee, the Grain Company, completed the procedures for collecting the goods at Maoming Railway Station and then went to the Supply Cooperative Line with the consignment note to pick up the goods. The Supply Cooperative Line also used the consignment note as the basis for delivery, indicating that the delivery and collection were acts based on the same transportation contract. Maoming Railway Station allocated the goods to the Supply Cooperative Line to enhance its capacity to receive and unload arriving goods. The temporary storage of the goods by the Supply Cooperative Line before delivery was an act performed as an agent of the carrier in the performance of the transportation contract. The handover of goods between Maoming Railway Station and the Supply Cooperative Line was a handover between the carrier and its agent. The failure of the carrier or its agent to correctly deliver the goods indicates that the transportation contract was not fully performed, and the resulting dispute should be a dispute over mistaken delivery in a railway cargo transportation contract. The consignee, the Grain Company, neither entrusted the Supply Cooperative Line to act as its agent in receiving the goods nor formed a de facto legal relationship of warehousing and storage with the Supply Cooperative Line. The storage fee paid by the Grain Company was a fee paid to the carrier in accordance with the Railway Law because the temporary storage of its goods exceeded the free storage period, and this fee falls within the category of transportation surcharges. The first and second instance courts incorrectly determined that an independent legal relationship of warehousing and storage had been established based on the fact that the Supply Cooperative Line had collected line usage and temporary storage fees for the goods.

The fraudulent obtaining of the transported goods in this case occurred when the Supply Cooperative Line was acting as agent for delivery. The Supply Cooperative Line should bear liability for damages. As the special line is part of the railway, acts within its transportation scope should be governed by the Railway Law. The existing evidence shows that the fraudulent obtainer took the goods using a forged consignment note. The Supply Cooperative Line could not distinguish the authenticity of the consignment note, and there is no other evidence to prove its gross negligence. Therefore, the mistaken delivery by the Supply Cooperative Line constituted ordinary negligence. By reference to the spirit of Article 2 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Cases of Compensation for Damages in Railway Transportation, the agent Supply Cooperative Line may enjoy the limitation of liability of the carrier. As the goods were transported with insured value, in accordance with Article 17, Paragraph 1, Item (1) of the Railway Law of the People's Republic of China, the Supply Cooperative Line shall compensate the Grain Company according to the insured amount and shall refund the storage and other fees collected. The Supply Cooperative Line's argument that it merely performed the delivery obligation on behalf of the carrier and should not bear liability is unfounded.

In summary, pursuant to Article 177, Paragraph 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Supreme People's Court makes the following judgment:

1. The civil judgments of the Guangdong High People's Court (1994) Yue Fa Jing Yi Shang Zi No. 155 and the Maoming Intermediate People's Court (1993) Mao Zhong Fa Jing Zi No. 39 are reversed.

2. The Maoming Supply and Marketing Cooperative Union Railway Special Line Business Department shall compensate the Maoming Grain Bureau Grain and Oil Materials Company for the loss of goods in the amount of RMB 139,000 according to the insured value, and shall pay delayed performance damages at a daily interest rate of 0.05% for the period from June 20, 1993, to October 20, 1994, amounting to RMB 33,360; and refund transportation surcharges of RMB 2,412.20 (including temporary storage fees). Deducting the amount already executed in the original instance of RMB 232,072, the Maoming Grain Bureau Grain and Oil Materials Company shall return to the Maoming Supply and Marketing Cooperative Union Railway Special Line Business Department RMB 57,299.80, and pay interest on the bank's current floating loan rate for the same period from February 9, 1995, until the date of full payment.

The first-instance and second-instance case acceptance fees are each RMB 5,538, of which the Maoming Supply and Marketing Cooperative Union Railway Special Line Business Department shall bear RMB 3,888.48 each, and the Maoming Grain Bureau Grain and Oil Materials Company shall bear RMB 1,649.52 each.
